title: Micro-cohort continuous scheduler with soft-KV compression and slab-aware preemption
creator: Avery Chen
description: Design and implement a micro-cohort continuous scheduler that groups concurrent requests into small, length-aware cohorts and applies a soft-KV-compression policy and slab-aware preemption to reduce GPU memory fragmentation and improve throughput for mixed prompt/response workloads. The goal is to lower p95 token latency for tail-heavy dialogues while improving overall token/s GPU efficiency and avoiding catastrophic KV thrashing under bursty traffic.
acceptance_criteria: P95 token latency improves by >= 8% for mixed prompt/response test traces compared to baseline continuous-batcher-1.18
Average GPU memory fragmentation (measured by free slab ratio) reduced by >= 12% on synthetic skewed-dialogue workloads
End-to-end throughput (tokens/s) improves or remains within 3% of baseline for steady load while tail latency improves
No regression in correctness or cache-provided responses (existing unit/integration tests pass)
Feature flag controlled rollout with canary traffic and automatic rollback on SLO breach
design_decisions: Use micro-cohort grouping: cohort_size = min(8, concurrent_requests) and cohort_max_seq_ratio = 2.0 to tolerate short/long mixing without excessive padding
Introduce soft-KV-compression (SQC): compress idle KV entries older than 90s with lightweight quantized snapshot to reduce slab residency while keeping decompression latency under 1.5ms on GPU
Slab-aware preemption: when free_slab_ratio < 18%, preempt lowest-priority micro-cohort (LRU by arrival+length) instead of evicting cold KV immediately
Backpressure policy: when preemption occurs, mark related routes with temporary 'slot-throttle' which reduces cohort admission rate for 250ms windows
Telemetry hooks: add cohort_id and kv_compression_state to trace spans to correlate preemption with latency spikes
progress_updates: 2025-02-20: Kickoff meeting with infra, runtime, and platform. Agreed on micro-cohort concept and SQC prototype scope.
2025-02-24: Prototype KV compression encoder landed (PR #4578) — basic FP16 delta encoding for older KV pages. Microbench: encode/decode ~1.2ms on GA100.
2025-02-27: Scheduler shim implemented to assign cohort_id and enforce cohort_size. Early offline sim shows 6% p95 improvement on our mixed-dialogue replay.
2025-03-01: Added slab-aware preemption logic and unit tests for preemption invariants. Observed decrease in free_slab_ratio fragmentation in local cluster runs.
2025-03-03: Integration run against canary trace shows a 9% p95 improvement and 14% reduction in fragmentation; however, saw rare decompress spikes at 1.8ms — investigating.
2025-03-03: Follow-up action: tune compression watermark and add adaptive decompression timeout to avoid tail amplification.
tradeoffs: SQC adds a small CPU/GPU decompression cost; we accept rare ~1.5–2.0ms decompress spikes to gain sustained memory footprint reduction and better batching efficiency
Smaller cohorts reduce padding overhead but slightly reduce packing efficiency for very short-only workloads; mitigated by cohort_max_seq_ratio and dynamic resizing heuristic
Slab-aware preemption favors throughput and tail latency at the cost of preempted requests being scheduled later — we mitigate by limiting preemption frequency and preferring low-cost cohorts
Added complexity to tracing and rollback mechanisms (feature-flag gated) to ensure safe rollout across Dedicated and Private deployments
testing_plan: Unit tests for cohort assignment, eviction ordering, and SQC state transitions
Integration tests using mixed-turn replay traces (customer-like): short-long, long-short, and tail-heavy bursts
Performance perf-run on canary cluster with GA100 and A100 pools measuring p50/p95/p99 tokens latency and free_slab_ratio over 24h
Chaos test: enforced KV eviction storms + bursty arrivals to validate preemption/backpressure behavior
Gradual rollout: start at 1% hosted API traffic, watch SLOs and cost metrics, expand cohorts to 10/25/100% if stable
implementation_notes: Cohort metadata embedded in request enqueuer; keep cohort state in lightweight ring buffer on worker to avoid cross-worker locking
SQC snapshots will use existing quantization library with a 2-tier format: fast lossy snapshot for warm entries + full-lossless for cold entries older than 15m
Expose runtime knobs: cohort_size, cohort_max_seq_ratio, compression_age_s, free_slab_preempt_threshold, preempt_cooldown_ms
Add circuit-breaker metric 'kv_preempt_events' to Console with alert when > 10/min per node
Ensure Private deployment has toggles for SQC due to compliance concerns around in-memory compressed representations
open_risks: Decompression spikes causing p99 regressions under extremely bursty workloads — mitigated by adaptive decompression timeouts and fallbacks to eviction
Edge cases where compressed KV snapshots interact poorly with quantized kernels — will run cross-model sanity checks
Operational complexity for Dedicated customers with tight capacity guarantees — plan: opt-out via org-level feature flag and manual rollout assistance
notes: Follow-up: schedule ops runbook entry for preemption incidents and rollback steps
Coordinate with SDK team to add cohort debug header for reproduction in customer support flows
Post-mortem if decompression p99 > 3ms in canary — include timeline and mitigation steps
